title: Diagnostic: A Range That Can't Exist
hints: Keep the `Range<Int>` annotation but change the literal to the closed-range operator.
jsBridge: JS has no range types. Swift distinguishes `Range` (`a..<b`) from `ClosedRange` (`a...b`) at the type level. The two can't hold each other's literals, which is why generic code uses `RangeExpression`.

compass.q: Why are `Range` and `ClosedRange` separate types rather than one type with a flag? What would the flag cost?
`5...1` compiles but crashes at runtime. Why can't the compiler catch it?
APIs like `array[range]` accept `RangeExpression`. Why does that let you pass `2...`, `..<5` and `1...3` to the same subscript?
TS could model ranges with branded types. Would that catch `5...1`? What's special about what Swift checks at compile time?
